problem: The answer says the objective function 'may lower its rank'. In RPL, rank counts distance from the root, so a node whose parent link turns lossy must move to a higher rank (further from the root), not a lower one. A student copying 'lower its rank' into the exam writes the opposite of what happens, and it also contradicts Q6, where moving one hop away raises rank by one.
fix: The link looks lossy, so its cost in the objective function rises. RPL may then move the node to a higher rank (further from the root in cost terms) or switch it to a different parent with better link quality; retransmissions add delay and control overhead.

problem: E3 is drawn as a child of R2, which is at rank 1, yet E3 is labelled rank 3, skipping rank 2. Q6 in the same chapter teaches that under a hop-count objective a child of a rank-1 node gets rank 2. The figure and the quiz contradict each other, and the caption's 'rank rises as nodes move away from the root' does not explain a jump of two.
fix: Either label E3 as rank 2 (child of the rank-1 router R2), or add a rank-2 node between R2 and E3 and note that this DODAG's objective function adds more than one rank unit per hop.

problem: 'Some syllabi call 6LoWPAN IPv6 over Low-Power Wireless Personal Area Networks' presents the standard full form as if it were an optional syllabus variant. Students may think the expansion is one of several competing names.
fix: 6LoWPAN stands for IPv6 over Low-Power Wireless Personal Area Networks. It is an adaptation layer, not a routing protocol.

problem: 'IPHC sends a short tag and the changing fields' reuses the word tag, which this chapter already uses for the fragmentation datagram_tag, so the two mechanisms look alike. IPHC has no tag: it sends a dispatch byte plus bit flags that mark which header fields are elided and which are carried in compressed form.
fix: IPHC sends one dispatch byte and a set of bit flags saying which fields are omitted or compressed, plus the few fields that actually change; the receiver rebuilds the full 40-byte IPv6 header from those flags.
